key_insight: Resistive MHD simulations show that an imposed flow mimicking a collapsing Navier–Stokes core can trigger magnetic reconnection that splits a flux ring into daughter rings.
engineering_relevance: The results connect intense fluid collapse to magnetic topology changes, potentially informing models of reconnection in conducting fluids and plasmas.
method: Drive a magnetic ring with a regularized flow reproducing the collapsing core’s geometry and scaling.
Remove the imposed drive at the nominal singular time and track subsequent resistive MHD evolution.
Analyze poloidal-flux bifurcations and Lorentz feedback, with three-dimensional simulations checking persistence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter-free cusp predictions of daughter-ring asymmetry for single-island splits, while three-dimensional simulations retain splitting and merger.
watch_item: The simulations impose a regularized collapse-like flow rather than establish a self-consistent Navier–Stokes singularity.
paper_title: Magnetic flux ring splitting near a Navier-Stokes singularity
